sources.entry: pudb - A full-screen, console-based Python debugger.

summary.one_liner: PuDB is a full-screen, console-based visual debugger for Python that runs in a terminal.
summary.what_it_does: PuDB shows syntax-highlighted source, the stack, breakpoints, and variables together in one terminal screen, updated as the program runs. Variable displays can be expanded, collapsed, and customized. Navigation uses single keystrokes, supporting cursor keys and Vi shortcuts, with other keys modeled on pdb commands. Users can search source code, browse and reload loaded modules, set breakpoints by pointing at a line and pressing "b", and run to a cursor line with "t". It also offers a Python shell in the current environment ("!"), a command prompt beside the source ("Ctrl-X"), and a post-mortem mode for exceptions. The README also mentions pre-bundled light and dark themes, remote control from a separate terminal, and IPython integration.
use_cases: debug a Python script in the terminal
inspect variables and the call stack visually
post-mortem debugging of a crashed program
set and manage breakpoints without a GUI
debug over SSH or in a console-only environment
notable: Full-screen terminal UI showing source, stack, breakpoints, and variables at once
Single-keystroke navigation with Vi and cursor-key support
Post-mortem mode with emphasis on exception handling
Drop to a Python shell in the current environment with '!'
Can be controlled from a separate terminal
caveats: README does not include installation or run instructions beyond a git clone command
Python 2.7 is supported only in versions 2019.2 and older
Requires a terminal environment; it is not a GUI debugger
